name: Justice Bolick
description: Concurred, arguing that the initiative is legislative in nature and therefore a proper matter for the City's voters to decide under the Arizona Constitution.

name: Vice Chief Justice Lopez
description: Concurred, argued that the statute's double counting of invalid signatures unconstitutionally raised the initiative signature threshold, violating both the Arizona and United States Constitutions.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that the Free and Equal Elections Clause is implicated when voters are disenfranchised or votes are given unequal weight, but found no underlying constitutional right to vote in every court of appeals judge's retention election, and the one-person, one-vote principle does not apply to judicial elections.

name: Jennifer M. Perkins
description: Concurred, delivered the decision of the Court, finding the offering was exempt from registration, some fraud claims were puffery or had a reasonable basis, but upholding the fraud finding for personal use of funds.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, argued that Arizona law does not permit FDA black box warnings to substitute for expert testimony to establish the standard of care in medical malpractice cases.

name: BOLICK, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the failure to follow the black box warning under the facts presented constitutes a prima facie case of negligent failure to warn, making dismissal inappropriate.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature intended to hold GEI defendants criminally responsible for their actions, making them liable for victim restitution, and overruled Heartfield.

name: Justice Bolick
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the court, finding that release time provisions violate the Gift Clause but not free-speech, free-association, or right-to-work rights.

name: JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, arguing that the 2018 legislative amendments reclassified desegregation expenses as a new type of secondary property tax not eligible for state reimbursement, and these amendments are constitutional.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that trial courts must apply the Gomez factors to determine whether to disqualify a prosecutor's office when an employee is a victim, balancing defendant's due process and victim's constitutional rights.

name: TIMMER, VICE CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that a higher bid is relevant but not conclusive for Gift Clause analysis, and non-pecuniary factors are important. Also, found disputed facts regarding the City's discretion in canceling the RFP, requiring remand.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, authored the Opinion of the Court, arguing that the Condominium Act did not effect a taking of the Xias' property due to contractual agreement, but that § 33-1228(C) required the sale of all condominium property, not just individual units, if any portion was to be sold.

name: JUSTICE KING
description: Concurred, argued that the State has a right to appeal expungement orders affecting its substantial rights under § 13-4032(4), and § 36-2862(F) does not preclude this right.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that § 36-2322 does not create a right to abortion or repeal the older ban, § 13-3603, which is now enforceable after Roe v. Wade was overturned.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that § 36-2322 and § 13-3603 should be harmonized, allowing abortions up to fifteen weeks or to preserve the woman's health, and that the majority incorrectly used a session law note to create ambiguity.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Dissented with Vice Chief Justice Timmer's opinion.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, argued that the anti-abrogation clause does not extend to dram-shop actions because they were recognized after statehood.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the decision correctly upholds legislative authority in tort law and prevents the judiciary from overstepping its bounds by creating new liabilities.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the anti-abrogation clause protects common law actions as they evolve, including dram-shop actions, and the legislature's limitation unconstitutionally abrogates this right.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented in part and in the result, arguing that the majority's 'substantial probability' standard for direct disclosure is an additional, inconsistent requirement that impermissibly diminishes a defendant's ability to exercise a federal constitutional right, and that the 'reasonable possibility' standard should apply consistently.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented in part and in the result, arguing that the majority's 'substantial probability' standard for direct disclosure is an additional, inconsistent requirement that impermissibly diminishes a defendant's ability to exercise a federal constitutional right, and that the 'reasonable possibility' standard should apply consistently.

name: BOLICK, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the court of appeals erred by concluding it did not have appellate jurisdiction over the dismissal of resentencing proceedings, as these were direct appeals affecting substantial rights and the constitutional right to appeal.

name: JUSTICE BEENE
description: Concurred, argued that before a defendant's right to appeal can be abrogated under § 13-4033(C), the defendant must receive notice, the waiver must be knowing, intelligent, and voluntary, and the defendant must be provided an opportunity at sentencing to prove their absence was involuntary.

name: BOLICK, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that A.R.S. § 23-1043.01(B) is constitutional because the original public meaning of "injury by accident" in the Arizona Constitution did not encompass mental stress injuries, and the legislature permissibly expanded workers' compensation within limits.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that A.R.S. § 23-1043.01(B) violates Article 18, Section 8 of the Arizona Constitution because "injury" and "personal injury" should be interpreted to include mental injuries, and the statute impermissibly restricts legal causation.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the Arizona Constitution grants individual commissioners investigatory powers, including the authority to issue subpoenas, and that a majority cannot prevent an individual commissioner from exercising these powers.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission did not prevent Burns from exercising his investigatory powers, as his actions were part of a contested rate case subject to the Commission's plenary authority, not an independent investigation under section 4.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the court, finding that a unit number is not required in a residence address and that signatures should not be disqualified for the affidavit issue due to the Secretary's impossible compliance procedures, upholding the constitutional right to the initiative process.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that tax revenue measures for state support and maintenance are exempt from referendum, regardless of revenue increase or decrease.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Dissented, argued that tax revenue measures are only exempt from referendum if they meet all constitutional emergency measure requirements, which SB 1828 failed to do.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that legislative privilege protects communications related to legislative investigations, such as the election audit, as long as they are legislative in nature and not purely administrative or political, and that proving indirect impairment is not required.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, argued that the Arizona Constitution guarantees due process rights for individuals under grand jury investigation, requiring prosecutors to present clearly exculpatory evidence, including that related to justification defenses, to ensure a fair and impartial grand jury proceeding.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court affirming Robinson's convictions and sentences.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that attorney fees are recoverable as restitution only when reasonably necessary to remedy the harm directly caused by criminal conduct, and most of C.C.'s fees were not directly caused by Reed's conduct.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged budget reconciliation bills violated the Arizona Constitution's title requirement and single subject rule because their substantive provisions lacked a natural connection to their titles and budgetary purpose.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the "manageable standards" inquiry in the political question context is not constitutionally mandated and abdicates the judiciary's central role in determining constitutional boundaries.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that a crime victim has a constitutional and statutory right to be heard on the merits of a defendant's motion for a delayed appeal of a restitution order, based on the Victims' Bill of Rights.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision improperly broadens victims' rights beyond what is contemplated by the constitution and statutes, effectively conferring party status on victims in post-conviction relief proceedings.

name: JUSTICE Andrew W. Gould
description: Other, participated in oral argument but retired before the opinion was issued.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, finding Prop. 208's direct funding unconstitutional if it exceeds expenditure limits and that the Tax Enactment Clause does not apply to voter initiatives.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreeing with the denial of the preliminary injunction but disagreeing with the majority's severability analysis and the framework for determining unconstitutionality, arguing it almost certainly dooms the measure.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BRUTINEL
description: Concurred, argued that Arizona has not consented to federal damages liability under the FLSA because the legislature has not unequivocally expressed such consent.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that a standard of care expert affidavit is not required for ineffective assistance of counsel claims, Perry v. New Hampshire did not constitute a significant change in Arizona law, and A.R.S. § 13-4234(G) unconstitutionally conflicts with Arizona Rule of Criminal Procedure 32.4 by curtailing the right to appeal for IAC claims.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that Mesnard is immune for the investigatory report as it was a legislative function, but not for the news release which was a political act.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Concurred, argued that the case should be resolved on political question grounds, not speech or debate grounds, because the Constitution commits disciplinary functions solely to the legislature, making it nonjusticiable.

name: JUSTICE MONTGOMERY
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutional right to receive restitution guarantees the full amount of economic loss or injury caused by criminal conduct, rendering the statutory limitation unconstitutional.

name: Justice Andrew W. Gould
description: Did not take part in the drafting of the opinion due to retirement before issuance.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, argued that the home rule charter provision grants charter cities autonomy over purely municipal concerns, and the decision of whether to hold municipal elections on-cycle or off-cycle is a matter of purely municipal concern.

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented, argued that the majority misinterpreted the home rule charter provision by engrafting statutory and common law distinctions onto the constitutional text, which clearly states that a city's charter is subject to state laws.

name: VICE CHIEF JUSTICE TIMMER
description: Concurred, arguing that the City's payments to a private entity for economic development violated the Gift Clause because the value received by the public was far exceeded by the consideration paid, constituting an impermissible subsidy.

name: JUSTICE LOPEZ
description: Concurred, argued that neither the federal nor Arizona constitutions require a warrant for IP addresses and ISP subscriber information, as it falls under the third-party doctrine and is not a "private affair."

name: JUSTICE BOLICK
description: Dissented, argued that the Arizona Constitution's private affairs clause offers broader protections than the Fourth Amendment, requiring a warrant for IP addresses and ISP subscriber information.
